words.definition: To honor and remember an important person or event through a ceremony or action.
words.example: Every year the town gathers at dawn to commemorate the soldiers who never came home.
words.mnemonic: Break it up: co- (together) + memor (mindful, as in memory) + -ate — a group brings a memory to mind together.

words.definition: To keep the remembrance of a person or event alive, often with a lasting structure or record.
words.example: They memorialized the fallen firefighters with a bronze statue outside the station.
words.mnemonic: You take a 'memorial' and -ize it — turn a feeling of remembrance into a permanent thing.

words.definition: A bittersweet longing for happier times or places from earlier in life.
words.example: Hearing that old summer song filled her with nostalgia for her grandmother's porch.
words.mnemonic: From Greek nostos (homecoming) + algos (pain) — the sweet ache to return home.

words.definition: To talk or think fondly about pleasant experiences from the past.
words.example: The old friends sat by the fire and reminisced about their college road trips.
words.mnemonic: Sounds like 'remind us' — the stories remind us of who we used to be.

words.definition: To bring a past fact or experience back into the mind.
words.example: She frowned, trying to recollect exactly where she had left her keys the night before.
words.mnemonic: re- + collect: you go back and 'collect' scattered pieces of the past again.

words.definition: A looking back at events that already happened, judged from the present.
words.example: In retrospect, quitting that safe job to start the bakery was the smartest thing he ever did.
words.mnemonic: retro- (backward) + -spect (look) — the same 'spect' as inspect; you look backward.

words.definition: All the people who will live in future generations.
words.example: The author kept meticulous journals so that posterity could understand daily life in her era.
words.mnemonic: Like 'posterior' — what comes after and behind you: the generations that follow.

words.definition: The sequence of family members from whom a person is descended.
words.example: He proudly traced his lineage back to a family of shipbuilders in the 1700s.
words.mnemonic: line + age — a family 'line' followed down through the ages.

words.definition: Belonging to or inherited from family members who lived in earlier generations.
words.example: The family returned to their ancestral village to see the stone house their great-grandparents built.
words.mnemonic: You can see 'ancestor' hiding inside it — anything of the ancestors.

words.definition: An object made by humans, especially one of historical or cultural interest.
words.example: The museum displayed a cracked clay pot and other artifacts dug from the ancient city.
words.mnemonic: From Latin arte factum, 'made by skill' — art + fact = a thing crafted by human hands.

words.definition: Something that serves as clear proof or evidence of a quality or fact.
words.example: The bridge, still standing after two centuries, is a testament to its builders' skill.
words.mnemonic: Shares a root with 'testify' — it testifies, standing as proof of something true.

words.definition: A structure built to honor a notable person or event.
words.example: Tourists gathered around the towering stone monument dedicated to the city's founder.
words.mnemonic: From Latin monere, 'to remind' (like 'admonish') — a big structure that reminds everyone.

words.definition: A collection of historical documents or records kept for reference.
words.example: The journalist spent weeks in the newspaper's archive hunting for articles from 1950.
words.mnemonic: Sounds like 'ark hive' — an ark that shelters records in an orderly hive of shelves.

words.definition: A written record of events arranged in order, year by year.
words.example: That impossible comeback earned the team a permanent place in the annals of the sport.
words.mnemonic: From Latin annus, 'year' (like 'annual') — history kept one year at a time.

words.definition: A written account of the author's own life and personal experiences.
words.example: In her memoir, the retired diplomat revealed secrets from decades of quiet negotiations.
words.mnemonic: From French mémoire — say it aloud and you hear 'memory'; a whole book of yours.

words.definition: To bring something back into your mind after having known it before.
words.example: Under pressure, she could barely recall her own phone number.
words.mnemonic: re- (again) + call: you 'call back' a memory from storage.

words.definition: The state of being completely forgotten, or of noticing nothing at all.
words.example: The once-famous singer faded into oblivion after his final album flopped.
words.mnemonic: Sounds like 'oblivious' — both mean blank, unaware, gone from notice.

words.definition: A condition in which a person loses part or all of their memory.
words.example: After the car crash, he suffered amnesia and couldn't name his own children.
words.mnemonic: a- (without) + -mnesia (memory, as in 'mnemonic') = without memory.

words.definition: To rub out or remove something so it can no longer be seen.
words.example: Years of rain had effaced the names carved on the old gravestones.
words.mnemonic: ef- + face: strip the 'face' or surface markings clean off something.

words.definition: To protect an idea or right and treat it as very special or sacred.
words.example: The right to free speech is enshrined in the country's constitution.
words.mnemonic: en- + shrine: place something inside a shrine, keeping it holy and safe.

words.definition: A long, distinct period of history marked by notable events or features.
words.example: The invention of the printing press opened a new epoch in human communication.
words.mnemonic: Sounds like 'epic' — an epic, sweeping stretch of time.

words.definition: An earlier action or decision used as a guide for similar situations later.
words.example: The court's ruling set a precedent that judges would follow for decades.
words.mnemonic: pre- (before) + -cedent (going, as in 'proceed'): something that goes before.

words.definition: Clear understanding of a situation only after it has already happened.
words.example: In hindsight, selling the house before the crash was a brilliant move.
words.mnemonic: hind (rear/behind) + sight: seeing clearly by looking backward.

words.definition: The ability to predict what will happen and prepare for it in advance.
words.example: Her foresight in buying extra supplies saved the team when the storm hit.
words.mnemonic: fore (before) + sight: seeing ahead of the event, not after it.

words.definition: Bringing to mind something from the past because of a close similarity.
words.example: The smell of the bakery was reminiscent of her grandmother's kitchen.
words.mnemonic: Cousin of 'reminisce' — it tugs you back toward old memories.

words.definition: Deserving great respect because of age, wisdom, or long service.
words.example: The venerable professor had taught at the university for over fifty years.
words.mnemonic: Root of 'venerate' (to worship) — someone worthy of veneration.

words.definition: To support or maintain a law, decision, or principle so it continues.
words.example: The higher court chose to uphold the original verdict.
words.mnemonic: up + hold: hold something up so it doesn't collapse or fall.

words.definition: To formally accuse someone of committing a serious crime.
words.example: A grand jury voted to indict the executive on charges of fraud.
words.mnemonic: Say it 'in-DITE' — you write someone 'in' to a criminal charge.

words.definition: To offer facts or reasons as proof to support an argument.
words.example: The lawyer adduced several documents to prove her client's innocence.
words.mnemonic: ad- (toward) + -duce (to lead, as in 'produce'): lead facts toward your point.

words.definition: To make something stronger or better able to resist attack.
words.example: Soldiers worked through the night to fortify the town's walls.
words.mnemonic: Hear 'fort' inside it — turn a place into a sturdy fort.

words.definition: Concerned with using language for persuasive or striking effect rather than genuine meaning.
words.example: Her rhetorical question hung in the air, and no one was expected to answer it.
words.mnemonic: Sounds like 'rhetor' — the ancient Greek public speaker trained to sway a crowd with words.

words.definition: To publicly ridicule a person using humor, mockery, or biting satire.
words.example: The cartoonist lampooned the mayor, drawing him as a bumbling clown tripping over his own promises.
words.mnemonic: Sounds like 'harpoon' — a satirist harpoons a public figure with sharp jokes.

words.definition: A subtle, underlying quality, feeling, or meaning hidden beneath the surface.
words.example: There was an undertone of anger in his calm, carefully measured reply.
words.mnemonic: under + tone — a tone running underneath whatever is openly being said.

words.definition: The level of formality in language chosen to suit a particular situation or audience.
words.example: She shifted into a formal register the moment the job interview began.
words.mnemonic: A cash register picks the exact amount; a language register picks the exact level of formality.

words.definition: A speaker or writer's particular choice and arrangement of words and phrases.
words.example: The poet's precise diction made every single line feel carefully deliberate.
words.mnemonic: Shares its root with 'dictionary' (Latin dicere, to say) — it's about which words you pick to say.

words.definition: A small amount of something that stays behind after the main part is gone.
words.example: A sticky residue coated the pan after all the syrup had boiled away.
words.mnemonic: re- (back) + 'sit' (settle) — what settles back and lingers behind.

words.definition: A person who held a job or position before someone else took it over.
words.example: The new principal continued the reforms her predecessor had begun years earlier.
words.mnemonic: pre- (before) + '-cessor' (goer) — the one who goes before you into the role.

words.definition: The act of holding a person or event in the mind, often to honor them.
words.example: They planted an oak tree in remembrance of the soldiers who never came home.
words.mnemonic: Hidden inside is 'member' — reassembling the members, or pieces, of the past in your mind.

words.definition: A sorrowful poem or song written to mourn someone who has died.
words.example: The composer wrote an elegy for his late mentor, every note heavy with grief.
words.mnemonic: From Greek 'elegos', a mournful song — picture a lone violin ('e-LEG-y') playing beside a grave.

words.definition: To express deep sorrow, grief, or regret about something openly.
words.example: The farmers lamented the drought that had withered their crops for a second year.
words.mnemonic: Sounds like 'la-moan' — a long, drawn-out moan of sorrow.

words.definition: To weaken something or make it less effective, often quietly or indirectly.
words.example: His sarcastic tone completely undercut the sincerity of the apology he was offering.
words.mnemonic: under + cut — to cut the ground out from beneath something, weakening it.

words.definition: To bring something to the front so it receives the most attention.
words.example: The essay foregrounds the voices of women that traditional history usually ignores.
words.mnemonic: fore (front) + ground — the patch of ground nearest the viewer, the part you notice first.

words.definition: A picture or description that exaggerates someone's features for comic or mocking effect.
words.example: The street artist drew a caricature of the tourist with an enormous nose and tiny body.
words.mnemonic: From Italian 'caricare', to load — a face loaded up with exaggerated features.

words.definition: To describe something as larger, better, or worse than it truly is.
words.example: He overstated his role, claiming he had run a project he had merely joined late.
words.mnemonic: over + state — to state something over the top, pushing it beyond the truth.

words.definition: To describe something as smaller or less important than it actually is.
words.example: Calling the hurricane 'a bit of wind,' she badly understated the danger heading their way.
words.mnemonic: under + state — to state something under the truth, deliberately playing it down.

words.definition: Overly concerned with tiny rules and formal details, often to flaunt one's own learning.
words.example: Her pedantic supervisor returned the report twice over a single misplaced comma.
words.mnemonic: Sounds like 'pedal antics' — picture a fussy instructor making a scene over exactly which foot-pedal you touched.

words.definition: Deeply affecting the emotions, especially stirring sadness or a bittersweet ache.
words.example: The old soldier's poignant letter to his late wife left the whole room in tears.
words.mnemonic: From Latin 'pungere' (to prick), the root of 'puncture' — such a moment pricks your heart like a pin.

words.definition: Bringing strong images, memories, or feelings vividly to mind.
words.example: The evocative smell of woodsmoke instantly carried her back to childhood campfires.
words.mnemonic: Break it into 'e-' (out) + 'voc' (voice), as in 'vocal' — it calls old memories out of you.
